newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aides accused of possible false statements.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aides accused of possible false statements.

text.p: A Republican-controlled select House of Representatives subcommittee accused Clinton administration officials on Thursday of making possibly criminal false statements on U.S. policy on Iran arming the Bosnians in 1994.

A Republican subcommittee member accused President Bill Clinton's administration of lying to allies, Congress and the U.S. public. Congressional Democrats called the allegation outrageous and unsupported.

An unclassified summary of the subcommittee's "Top Secret" report said that "several administration officials gave false testimony to Congress on the development and implementation of the Iranian green light policy...
"The subcommittee is referring this matter to the Department of Justice for further criminal investigation."

Democrats issued a statement saying the finding was outrageous because U.S. officials disagreed only on details. They said the officials agreed they decided neither to support nor oppose Iranian weapons for Bosnia in April 1994 because they feared Bosnia would collapse without the arms.
But Representative Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican, said: "The administration lied to our allies...They lied to the Congress of the United States and they lied to the American people."
